cells.tense: The shared thing you keep going is being seen, and the credit is landing where it belongs.
cells.ask: Go to one gathering and speak well of something that works there — no name attached, just the thing itself, the way it is done.
cells.core:
You've carried something for the group — the way it is done, the reason it is kept — and people keep it running through you. That is not vanity. It is the circle closing: what you gave quietly is visible now, and you are letting it be visible.

The risk is going stiff when it lands. You can take the good of it without turning care into performance, or into an identity you then have to keep feeding. This ease does not maintain itself; it lasts by being passed on. Say plainly what you keep and why, and notice who picks it up unbidden. That is the work continuing without being pushed.

cells.verb: Have a sacrifice seen and honored by the group

cells.tense: You're bracing for a moment of recognition that hasn't come, building your case before anyone has asked.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you keep up for the group and study it for ten minutes — what works, what doesn't — and tell no one.
cells.core:
You're tending the shared thing with an eye out ahead — earning the moment it gets noticed, spending yourself before anyone asked. Somewhere up there, the room finally sees it, and each move bends toward that. It's costing you the thing itself.

Bracing like this isn't selfish, but it slips out into the open. Watch for the evening you spend describing what you've done instead of doing it. The correction isn't doing less. It's looking closely until you can tell which efforts belong to the group and which belong to your need to be seen making them. Careful attention, turned inward, is the fix. When you can tell those apart, the release is real — surrender as fulfillment, not defeat, because what you gave was never yours to keep.

cells.tense: Somewhere earlier the giving went unhonored, and you've stopped putting your work anywhere it could be looked at.
cells.ask: Do one concrete piece of the shared upkeep you'd normally skip — regular, unseen — fully, then tell one person you did it.
cells.core:
You know how to hold something for the group, and you've stopped putting it out. No announcement, no offering — quieter than that, work that no longer gets brought where it can be received. What you know hasn't gone anywhere; the showing has.

What has run dry gives no lectures. Stay exact, and the way back comes through persistence — keep the practice when nobody is watching, and what you carry won't crush you. Test it with one small visible act. It teaches you the difference between offering that asks to be seen and giving that finds its footing. Either way, the upkeep continues.

cells.tense: You're carrying the shared thing forward through what you repeat and keep, and calling it just how things are done.
cells.ask: Name one thing you've done for the group's continuity that you'd usually call the tradition running itself, and take it as yours.
cells.core:
You already shape what the people near you value — in how you keep a practice, who you bring into it, what you let go of — and you describe it as the tradition doing its own work. The work is happening. Your name isn't on it.

This isn't about ego. It's about not standing in your own life as a giver. The shift from the older form of the same trend is growing something without forcing it. When something you hold is used well, take a second and register that you did that. The group carried the meaning; you carried the group across the rough part.

attempts.check: The record supports sacrifice being seen and honored at the group level; it does not say this person gave anything up, and it does not say their effort is going unacknowledged — the Too Little cell must locate the person behind the present without saying what happened there. The obvious reader objection is 'I never sacrificed anything, this isn't my story,' so every cell names the posture — tending the shared thing, being seen for it — and lets them reject the biography and keep the instruction. The asks survive being wrong because each is one physical act toward the shared thing itself (a good word in it, one fewer appearance, one plain account, one decision claimed as theirs), not a cure for a past. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line implying their private giving went unseen — cut from every version.
